briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Nepal's Catastrophic Floods and Himalayan Glacier Collapse: An Urgent Climate Crisis Warning
sections.content: In Nepal, record-breaking floods and landslides have resulted in 552 deaths and over 1,500 missing persons to date, with severe casualties reported, including bodies swept away by torrents and found over 150km away in India [5, 9, 11, 23, 77, 79]. This disaster is primarily attributed to glacier collapse and permafrost thaw caused by climate change. The recurrence of Himalayan glacier melt, which also occurred two years ago, serves as a stark warning about the repetitive and severe nature of climate crisis impacts [18, 19, 21, 24, 84, 86, 97]. Experts have expressed concerns that Himalayan rivers will become more turbulent due to climate change, leading to more floods and disasters. The local situation is critical, with rescue operations halted and residents evacuated due to the collapse of natural dam lakes formed by debris flows [10, 21, 78]. Employees from Korean companies such as Doosan Enerbility and Korea South-East Power have been isolated or lost contact, prompting the urgent dispatch of on-site response teams from the Korean government and corporations. However, access for rescue helicopters has been delayed due to flight restrictions imposed by local military authorities, leading to desperate pleas from families [80, 81, 82, 83]. This situation is being widely recognized internationally as a powerful warning about the consequences of climate change and the cost of inaction in the face of the climate crisis [89, 94, 110].

sections.title: ⚠️ Intensification of Global Climate Phenomena and Insufficient Adaptation Funding
sections.content: Research findings have been released indicating that climate change is further intensifying the 'super El Niño' phenomenon [13, 95, 101, 102, 103]. Coral studies have confirmed that human-induced climate change is making El Niño 36% stronger, with warnings that this could lead to an existential threat to food security [95, 96, 103]. Meanwhile, heat stress caused by climate change is disproportionately affecting children [100], and the role of global warming is becoming increasingly clear, as evidenced by the 'mega-drought' in the Colorado River basin since 2000, which has led to a river crisis [105]. Concurrently, Australian corporate disclosures have revealed insufficient funding for climate change adaptation, posing a significant challenge for companies worldwide, including those in Korea [4]. This intensification of global climate phenomena once again underscores the urgent need for immediate and comprehensive action on climate change.

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are actively underway to address climate change and achieve carbon neutrality [12, 26, 35, 48]. Gangjin County plans to invest 96.5 billion KRW to construct the Byeongyeongcheon Dam for climate change response [1], and international cooperation is also strengthening, with Ulsan Science University signing an academic exchange agreement with Uzbekistan's University of Environmental and Climate Change Research [2, 3, 14, 20]. At the local government level, carbon neutrality practices through citizen participation are expanding, including Nowon-gu's 'Carbon Neutrality Citizen Declaration' [26, 34, 37, 39], Anseong-si's 'Launch of the Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth Committee and Climate Citizen Participation Group' [35, 48, 51], and Dongdaemun-gu's pet plant-making initiatives [27, 41, 49]. In the renewable energy sector, movements for a major energy transition are gaining momentum, with the Korea Meteorological Administration and Korea Power Exchange strengthening cooperation on renewable energy weather information [52, 68], and Jeonbuk Self-Governing Province holding renewable energy policy discussions to explore region-led expansion [53, 56, 61, 66, 70, 72, 74, 76]. Furthermore, expectations are growing for the expansion of renewable energy supply and market revitalization, as the Korea Power Exchange prepares for the '2030 Renewable Energy 100GW Era' with the solar and wind power industries, and Korea Western Power explores renewable energy markets in Central Asia [54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 63, 64, 69, 71, 75].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 The Shadow of Carbon Neutrality Implementation: Challenges and New Conflicts
sections.content: Despite efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals having passed a turning point, concerns have been raised that the reduction of total greenhouse gas emissions remains an unresolved challenge [31]. Notably, the case of four K-entertainment companies, which emphasize carbon neutrality, showing up to a 15-fold increase in 'indirect carbon' emissions, highlights the importance of managing indirect emissions in corporate carbon neutrality implementation [30]. Furthermore, with AI data centers projected to expand to 18.4GW, concerns have been raised about potential conflicts between the 'Three Major Mega Projects' and carbon neutrality goals [44]. In the United States, awareness of the environmental impact of data centers is also spreading, with moratoriums being considered, indicating an emerging issue of balancing new technological development with environmental objectives [111]. In this context, the scope setting for greenhouse gases must be treated as a critical element in the concepts of carbon neutrality and net-zero [47], and alongside the recognition of Jinju City's carbon neutrality achievements, their verification also remains an important task [46]. Additionally, the amount of renewable energy curtailed due to output control is rapidly increasing, making it urgent to establish efficient operational plans alongside the expansion of renewable energy [60].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again reminds us of the severity of the climate crisis and the importance of global efforts to overcome it. This concludes the climate briefing for August 28, 2026.
